transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-25 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (Spectra), Alyssa Morgan (Spectra CTO), Jorge Ramirez (Spectra Infra)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown report. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency-sensitive scoring use case; security and SSO/KMS are blockers for procurement. Agreed to pilot with sample traffic and run cost simulation.

Topics:
- Console: per-route dashboards, token breakdown, latency percentiles
- Cost: per-route cost, batching/quantization levers, reserved capacity math
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs
- Next steps: pricing + pilot, perf benchmarks, procurement follow-up

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'll run through the console and cost stuff and Liam will jump in on the perf details, um, hope that's okay.
[00:08] Rajiv Patel: Yep, sounds good; Alyssa and Jorge are here too. Quick note, our timeline's tight — procurement wants vendor decision in two weeks.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Got it, two weeks. We'll focus on the parts that matter to procurement — security docs, cost, SSO and an initial perf read.
[00:25] Liam Ortiz: Hi all, i'll also show the per-route dashboards and how routing policies surface in the console.
[00:30] Alyssa Morgan: Great, main thing for us is predictable unit cost and control over latency. We run a scoring endpoint with 50 qps bursts and 100k tokens/day currently.
[00:41] Jorge Ramirez: And compliance — we need SOC2 plus KMS integration, and we host in a VPC for most of our infra.
[00:48] Maya Chen: Cool, we'll show Hosted, Dedicated and Private options. Ok i'm sharing my screen — landing page, overview, the usage analytics tab. Bear with me the screen share might be a little laggy.
[01:05] Liam Ortiz: So here on the per-route dashboard, you can pick a route — e.g., /scoring-v2 — and you get throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and per-token cost breakdown.
[01:18] Rajiv Patel: Per-token cost breakdown? how accurate is that?
[01:22] Liam Ortiz: It's based on the route's model selection, batching profile and the model unit cost — we estimate GPU time and amortize infra plus model license costs. It's an estimate but we've seen it be within 10-15% of billing in our pilots.
[01:35] Alyssa Morgan: Can we group by prompt type? We have different prompts for enrichment vs final scoring.
[01:40] Liam Ortiz: Yep, you can tag routes and the console supports breakdown by tag or annotation — we also have sampling to inspect example requests.
[01:48] Maya Chen: quick note — the sampling payloads sanitize PII by default for hosted customers, and for Private we leave it to your side but we provide options.
[01:57] Jorge Ramirez: How does KV cache and prefix caching show up in the analytics? we heavily rely on cache to reduce tokens.
[02:04] Liam Ortiz: Good question, we show cache hit rates as a metric on the route. We sometimes see transcription put K V cache as K V cash — so the metric name's cache_hit_rate. When prefix caching is active you'll see token consumption drop and a counter for saved tokens, that flows into the cost calc.
[02:22] Rajiv Patel: Ok that helps. What about the cost table — show pricing per million tokens?
[02:27] Maya Chen: In the cost breakdown view you'll see line items: model cost, infra overhead, caching savings, batching efficiency adjustments. You can toggle between hosted pricing and a reserved/dedicated estimate which replaces infra overhead with a commitment model.
[02:40] Alyssa Morgan: And quantization — does that change quality? we can't afford regression on scoring accuracy.
[02:47] Liam Ortiz: We provide recommended quantization profiles per model and a quality delta estimate based on our evals. For scoring you can pin a model + quantization profile and run A/B in the console to measure regressions against your golden prompts.
[02:58] Rajiv Patel: Sounds useful. Procurement will want to know about audit logs and key management.
[03:03] Maya Chen: For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM and we expose audit logs in the console with RBAC controls. For hosted we provide customer-isolated logs and options for log forwarding to your SIEM.
[03:15] Jorge Ramirez: SSO? SAML?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Yes SSO with SAML/Okta is supported, you'll get per-user RBAC and route-level permissions. We'll share our SSO guide.
[03:26] Alyssa Morgan: Competitors — have you seen folks compare this to OpenAI endpoints or Anthropic?
[03:31] Liam Ortiz: Yeah, customers often run a mix. Redwood's differentiation is per-route economics and the rollout + fallback policies — you can route by latency, cost or region and have automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if a higher-tier model is slow or unavailable.
[03:46] Rajiv Patel: Could you show the routing policy quickly?
[03:49] Liam Ortiz: Sure — going to the routing tab. here's a policy that sends <10ms-latency requests to an on-prem variant, otherwise falls back to hosted. You can set weights for A/B, and the console shows expected cost impact in-line.
[04:04] Maya Chen: On the cost side, here's an example cost-simulation we've built into the console — you input traffic profile, tokens per request, batching window, and it snapshots expected monthly spend across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[04:18] Jorge Ramirez: Do you require network peering for Private? We prefer VPC-peering or PrivateLink.
[04:24] Maya Chen: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and for on-prem we have an air-gapped option with a private control plane. We'll include network topology doc.
[04:35] Alyssa Morgan: Any SLA on percentiles? p99 is important for us.
[04:40] Liam Ortiz: Dedicated has SLA targets for p95 and p99 tail latency depending on instance type; hosted has region-backed SLOs. We can share the SLO table — i'll attach it.
[04:49] Rajiv Patel: For the pilot, what does Redwood need from us?
[04:52] Maya Chen: Sample traffic profile, a set of golden prompts for quality checks, and a small set of credentials for perf testing. We'll also need your procurement contact for contract review.
[05:02] Alyssa Morgan: We'll have procurement looped in if the numbers look solid.
[05:06] Liam Ortiz: quick sidebar — about token accounting, the console shows client-side vs server-side tokens, and the per-route cost uses server-side consumption; note that some SDKs trim whitespace differently so we recommend canonicalization to avoid surprises.
[05:22] Rajiv Patel: Any chance you can show an example of a cost-reduction suggestion from Redwood Optimize?
[05:27] Maya Chen: Sure, over in Optimize, we run heuristics and suggest batching windows, cache pins, or model swaps. here's a suggested change — move /enrich route to a quantized cheaper variant and increase batch window to 50ms; console sim shows 27% cost reduction and estimated quality delta ~0.3% on our evals.
[05:47] Alyssa Morgan: 0.3% might be acceptable but we need to validate on our golden set.
[05:52] Liam Ortiz: You can run a canary with the rollout tools and collect quality metrics in-line, compare to baseline.
[05:59] Jorge Ramirez: about data retention — logs older than 90 days are archived? we need 1 year for auditability.
[06:05] Maya Chen: For enterprise tiers we support configurable retention; for Private you control retention. We'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[06:13] Rajiv Patel: okay great. that addresses most items. On the pricing example, can you send an exportable spreadsheet of the sim?
[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes — Liam will run a tailored sim and we'll export a CSV with line items.
[06:25] Liam Ortiz: i'll need the tokens/request distribution and typical prompt lengths — Jorge if you can share that i'll run it today.
[06:32] Jorge Ramirez: i'll drop the traffic profile after the call.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Quick recap — we demoed per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, routing policies, and Optimize suggestions. Agreed next steps: Maya send pricing & pilot proposal, Liam run perf+cost sim, Jorge provide traffic profile, schedule procurement follow-up.
[06:52] Alyssa Morgan: Sounds good. Anything else?
[06:55] Rajiv Patel: no, thanks everyone.
[06:57] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up by end of week.
